fixtures: Files are copied into the run's data/ folder. A transcript file is the conversation so far; the run's reply is the assistant's next turn.

evals.name: opens-with-one-question
evals.prompt: We're designing multi-tenancy for our SaaS: how tenant data is isolated, how new tenants get provisioned, per-tenant configuration, and hooks into billing. They all affect each other. Help me think it through.
evals.expected_output: A short framing of what we're figuring out and why, then a single question on one decision point (most naturally data isolation, since the rest depend on it). No design, no recommendations across all four areas, no list of questions.
assertions: Before asking anything, briefly says what is being figured out and why
Asks the user exactly one question; there is no list or series of questions
The question is about a single decision point, not several of the four areas (isolation, provisioning, configuration, billing) at once
Does not lay out a design or recommendations covering the four areas

evals.name: acknowledges-and-builds
evals.prompt: Here's our conversation so far in data/sync-transcript.md. I've answered your first question, carry on.
evals.expected_output: Acknowledges the choice of content hashes and ties it to the user's reasons (clock drift, no server version counter). It may note in a sentence that hashes need the last-synced hash kept on each device, but it does not work out the sync mechanism (no case tables or step-by-step rules). Then one next question on a new decision point, such as what should happen when both devices edited a note, with options offered but no recommendation before the user answers.
assertions: Acknowledges the user's choice of content hashes, referring to their reason (clocks drift, or not wanting a server version counter)
Asks exactly one next question, on a new decision point rather than the comparison method again
Does not work out the sync mechanism for the user: no table or case-by-case rules for push, pull and conflict (a one- or two-sentence note of a consequence is fine)
Offers options for the next question, if any, without recommending or leaning toward one before the user answers

evals.name: closing-summary
evals.prompt: Our conversation so far is in data/sync-done-transcript.md. I think that covers it, go ahead.
evals.expected_output: Recognises the discussion is done and, before any design, lists back each decision as the user made it with their reason: content hashes for conflict detection (clocks drift, no server counter); keep both copies on a conflict (users would rather tidy a duplicate than lose text); an edit beats a delete, restoring the note with a "restored" banner. It invites corrections. A design may follow, but only after that standalone list, not with the decisions folded into the design's sections. No new questions on new topics.
assertions: Before any design, data model or code, gives a standalone list of the decisions made: content hashes, keep both copies on a conflict, and an edit beating a delete with a restored banner
Gives the user's reason with each decision, at least for hashes (clock drift or no server counter) and keeping both (not losing text)
Invites the user to correct the summary
Does not open new questions on topics the user has not raised
